The [NeuroML2 repository](https://github.com/NeuroML/NeuroML2) ships a canonical example suite: the tests the NeuroML community uses to decide whether a simulator implements the standard. TVB-O expresses every one of them as a single specification and checks the result against jNeuroML. This page is the scoreboard; each row links to the worked example behind it.

## What a LEMS experiment costs in XML

NeuroML splits a model across two file kinds. A `.nml` file defines reusable biological components (ion channels, cells, synapses, morphologies, networks) in a domain-specific schema:

```xml
<!-- NML2_SingleCompHHCell.nml (excerpt) -->
<ionChannelHH id="naChan" conductance="10pS" species="na">
  <gateHHrates id="m" instances="3">
    <forwardRate type="HHExpLinearRate" rate="1per_ms" midpoint="-40mV" scale="10mV"/>
    <reverseRate type="HHExpRate" rate="4per_ms" midpoint="-65mV" scale="-18mV"/>
  </gateHHrates>
</ionChannelHH>
```

A LEMS `.xml` file is the simulation harness: it includes the component files, wires them into a network, sets duration and step, and names what to record.

```xml
<!-- LEMS_NML2_Ex5_DetCell.xml (excerpt) -->
<Include file="Cells.xml"/>
<Include file="Networks.xml"/>
<Include file="Simulation.xml"/>
<Include file="../examples/NML2_SingleCompHHCell.nml"/>

<network id="net1">
  <population id="hhpop" component="hhcell" size="1"/>
</network>

<Simulation id="sim1" length="300ms" step="0.01ms" target="net1">
  <OutputFile id="of0" fileName="results/ex5.dat">
    <OutputColumn id="v" quantity="hhpop[0]/v"/>
  </OutputFile>
</Simulation>
```

A typical experiment therefore needs at least four files: three core includes that themselves import dozens more, the LEMS file, and one or more `.nml` models. The equations are nowhere in them; they live in `type` attributes pointing into the LEMS component-type hierarchy.

## What it costs in TVB-O

One document, with the equations in it. The FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillator of [Ex9](Ex9_FN.qmd):

```yaml
name: FitzHughNagumo
state_variables:
  V: {equation: {rhs: "V - V**3/3 - W + I"}}
  W: {equation: {rhs: "0.08 * (V + 0.7 - 0.8 * W)"}}
parameters:
  I: {value: 0.8}
integrator: {scheme: euler, dt: 0.01, duration: 200}
```

From that one spec, `exp.render("lems")` emits LEMS XML that jNeuroML runs, `exp.run()` simulates directly, and `exp.render("julia")` or `exp.render("pyrates")` targets another ecosystem entirely. See [LEMS export](../LEMS_Export.qmd) for the emitter and [IRI versus YAML](../IRI_vs_YAML.qmd) for how a component is referenced rather than copied.

## The conformance table

Each example is defined as a TVB-O `SimulationExperiment`, rendered to LEMS, run through jNeuroML as the reference, run again through `NeuroMLAdapter`, and compared trace by trace. The table below is read from the run record, so it reports what the last suite execution actually measured.

```{python}
#| label: conformance
#| echo: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

from IPython.display import Markdown

records = json.loads(Path("_run_all_examples_results.json").read_text())

# The suite's own grouping of the NeuroML2 examples by what each one exercises.
FAMILY = {
    "Ex0": "Single-cell ODE", "Ex2": "Single-cell ODE", "Ex8": "Single-cell ODE", "Ex9": "Single-cell ODE",
    "Ex1": "Conductance-based", "Ex5": "Conductance-based", "Ex22": "Conductance-based",
    "Ex4": "Channels & kinetics", "Ex10": "Channels & kinetics", "Ex15": "Channels & kinetics",
    "Ex18": "Channels & kinetics", "Ex24": "Channels & kinetics",
    "Ex3": "Synapses", "Ex6": "Synapses", "Ex7": "Synapses", "Ex20": "Synapses", "Ex21": "Synapses", "Ex27": "Synapses",
    "Ex12": "Networks", "Ex13": "Networks", "Ex19": "Networks", "Ex25": "Networks", "Ex26": "Networks",
    "Ex14": "Interchange", "Ex16": "Interchange", "Ex17": "Interchange", "Ex23": "Interchange",
}
ORDER = ["Single-cell ODE", "Conductance-based", "Channels & kinetics", "Synapses", "Networks", "Interchange"]
if any(r["name"] not in FAMILY for r in records):
    ORDER.append("Unclassified")

rows = ["| Family | Example | Traces | Worst $r$ | Worst NRMSE | Verdict |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|"]
for family in ORDER:
    members = [r for r in records if FAMILY.get(r["name"], "Unclassified") == family]
    for i, r in enumerate(sorted(members, key=lambda r: int(r["name"][2:]))):
        title = r["qmd"].removesuffix(".qmd").split("_", 1)[1].replace("_", " ")
        rows.append(
            f"| {family if i == 0 else ''} | [{r['name']} — {title}]({r['qmd']}) | {len(r['mappings'])} "
            f"| {r['worst_corr']:.6f} | {r['worst_nrmse']:.3g} | {r['status']} |"
        )

n = len(records)
passing = sum(r["status"] == "PASS" for r in records)
exact = sum(r["xml_exact_match"] for r in records)
Markdown(
    f"{passing} of {n} examples reproduce the jNeuroML reference; "
    f"{exact} of {n} render XML that is byte-identical to the canonical file.\n\n" + "\n".join(rows)
)
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Read the two columns together

The verdict is correlation-based: an example passes when its trace tracks the reference in shape. Two consequences are visible in the table above and neither is hidden.

**A scale error still passes.** [Ex22 (Pinsky-Rinzel)](Ex22_PinskyRinzel.qmd) reaches $r \approx 1$ with a worst NRMSE near 787. The waveform is right and the amplitude is not. Where the NRMSE column is not small, the example demonstrates structural agreement only.

**The XML is equivalent, not identical.** No example renders a byte-for-byte copy of the canonical file. TVB-O emits standard NeuroML2 component types that jNeuroML runs to the same result, which is the property that matters for interchange and the one the numerical columns measure.
:::

## Component examples

Alongside the LEMS simulation suite, the NeuroML2 repository ships component files that define models without running them. Each is expressed as a TVB-O object and re-emitted:

| | |
|---|---|
| Cells | [Abstract cells](NML2_AbstractCells.qmd) · [Single-compartment HH](NML2_SingleCompHHCell.qmd) · [Full cell](NML2_FullCell.qmd) · [Morphology](NML2_SimpleMorphology.qmd) |
| Channels | [Simple ion channel](NML2_SimpleIonChannel.qmd) |
| Synapses | [Synapse types](NML2_SynapseTypes.qmd) · [Analog synapses](NML2_AnalogSynapses.qmd) · [Gap junctions](NML2_GapJunctions.qmd) |
| Networks | [Inputs](NML2_Inputs.qmd) · [Instance-based network](NML2_InstanceBasedNetwork.qmd) · [Full NeuroML](NML2_FullNeuroML.qmd) |

## Running the suite yourself

```bash
pip install pyneuroml matplotlib scipy
python Interoperability/NeuroML/examples/_run_all_examples.py
```

jNeuroML runs the reference side and ships with pyNeuroML, so a working Java is the only extra requirement. The script rewrites `_run_all_examples_results.json`, and the table above follows.
